sections.html:
Elkhart County is in northern Indiana, right on the Michigan line. Its seat is Goshen, its biggest city is Elkhart, and the smaller towns are Middlebury, Nappanee, Bristol and Wakarusa. Population was 207,047 in 2020 and is estimated at 208,774 for 2025.

Two rivers shape where houses sit. The St. Joseph River is the main waterway, and the Elkhart River runs through Goshen and Dunlap before joining it in the city of Elkhart. A house near either river or on Simonton Lake brings drainage and insurance questions that a farm parcel near Nappanee does not.

Elkhart County calls itself the RV Capital of the World, and the recreational vehicle business drives local household budgets. When plants cut hours, a property tax installment is often one of the first bills to slip. That is how many owners here end up selling with taxes due.

The swings can be sharp. Manufacturing, which covers RV makers and their suppliers, held 49.6% of county jobs in April 2006, fell to 38.4% by April 2009, and climbed back to 46% by April 2016. Unemployment peaked at 18.9% in March 2009 and stood at 3.9% in April 2016. Those are decade-old figures, so read them as a pattern and not a current number. The pattern is why buyers and lenders here pay close attention to how long a house has sat and whether the taxes are current.

Three county offices share the job. Values and appeals sit with the assessor, tax cap credits are applied by the auditor, and the treasurer bills and collects. Your rate is built from every taxing unit over your parcel: county, city or town, school corporation and so on.

Circuit breaker caps hold your bill to a percentage of gross assessed value without touching the local rate. Anything the rate would charge above the cap is credited back by the auditor.

Property classCap on tax as share of gross assessed value
Homestead1%
Other residential, including rentals2%
Agricultural land2%
Nonresidential and personal property3%

You only get the 1% cap if the homestead standard deduction is on the parcel. Homestead status reaches the dwelling, a garage and one acre of land. Plenty of rural lots here are bigger, and the acreage beyond one falls in the 2% class. The state posts each county's budget order every January, and Elkhart County's 2026 order was issued January 15, 2026.

About a quarter of the parcels are reviewed each year, which means a new set of townships is looked at every cycle. In the 2024 phase, Baugo, Benton and Cleveland townships had residential and agricultural property reviewed, Concord had most districts reviewed in all classes, and York had commercial and exempt parcels reviewed.

The ratio study that checks those values drew on 2024 sales, January through December, and treated improved residential property township by township because every township had enough sales. A land order sent to the county board on December 3, 2024 took effect January 1, 2025.

  • Every sales disclosure form is checked through phone contacts, aerial maps, field visits, MLS records and CoStar.
  • Permits for all trades go into the county's assessment system. Elkhart, Goshen and Nappanee process their own permits, and the county handles the rest.

A permitted remodel or addition will show up in your assessment, so pull your property record card before listing and get any mistakes corrected early.

Appeals start with Form 130, filed with the Elkhart County assessor, and each parcel needs its own. The filing date is June 15, though the calendar year turns on the Form 11 notice. A notice mailed before May 1 puts the date in that same assessment year. A notice mailed May 1 or later pushes it to the year the tax bill goes out. Never got a notice? Then the tax bill itself serves as one.

Once your petition is in, the assessor sets up an informal sit-down to compare records. Failing that, the county Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals owes you a hearing inside 180 days, and you are entitled to 30 or more days of written warning. Want to move the date? You need good cause and a request filed 10 days or more beforehand. A no-show with no request can cost $50.

Unhappy with the ruling, or hearing nothing after 180 days? Take it to the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131. After that come the Indiana Tax Court and the Indiana Supreme Court. During the appeal, paying on last year's assessment keeps you penalty free, but paying less than that leaves the shortfall delinquent. The state's appeals fact sheet walks through each step.

Owing tax will not block a closing. Title companies simply collect the balance from your sale proceeds before cutting your check.

Delay raises the price. Indiana Code 6-1.1-37-10 sets the late charge at 5% when you pay inside 30 days of the due date and the parcel has a clean history. Any other late payment is hit with 10%. Each later installment date then adds 10% of the unpaid principal. Because that add-on is figured on the tax alone, earlier penalties do not compound it. Whatever you pay is applied to tax first, penalties second.

  • Request a payoff from the treasurer before you list or take an offer.
  • Confirm with the title company that both the spring and fall installments are covered.
  • Complete the sales disclosure form Indiana requires. A 2021 state memo said a sale closing by December 31 can set up the buyer's homestead deduction for the next year, with the disclosure form doubling as the application. Check current dates with the auditor.

Cash buyers who skip a lender can often close fast and buy the house as it stands, so no repair list and fewer showings. The overdue tax and penalties still come out of your proceeds, so know the figure up front.

Northern Indiana weather wears on roofs and basements. Goshen sees January lows near 17 degrees and July highs near 85, and Elkhart gets around 74 inches of snow a year.

Flooding has a record here. In February 2018 the Elkhart River in Goshen rose to a record 13.2 feet after heavy rain and snowmelt. More than 300 structures were damaged and some residents had to evacuate. If you have repaired water or storm damage, keep the receipts and permits. Buyers and inspectors ask about basement and drainage history on almost every house near the water.

Local buyers tend to ask about the school corporation before the street. Elkhart Community Schools covers most of Elkhart city. Concord Community Schools covers the southeast side of Elkhart and northwest Goshen, and Baugo Community Schools covers the southwest side. Goshen Community Schools covers most of Goshen, with small parts covered by Middlebury, Concord and WaNee.

The Indiana Toll Road follows the county's northern edge, with exits at Elkhart, Bristol and Middlebury. U.S. 20 follows the southern edge of Elkhart as the St. Joseph Valley Parkway, and U.S. 6, 33 and 131 also cross the county. The Goshen historic district, on the National Register since 1983, is built around the county courthouse, and older houses there may come with extra buyer questions about upkeep.

faqs.q: Who do I call about property tax in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: Start with the county treasurer for bills and payments and the county assessor for values and appeals. The treasurer's office is in the county building in Goshen. The state information center at 1-800-457-8283 also takes general property tax questions.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: The deadline is June 15, filed on Form 130 with the county assessor. Which year it falls in depends on whether the Form 11 notice was mailed before or after May 1. File a separate petition for each parcel.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Elkhart County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the unpaid tax and penalties from your proceeds at closing, so the amount comes off what you receive. Get a payoff figure from the treasurer first.

faqs.q: Why did my Elkhart County bill change when my value went up?
faqs.a: Circuit breaker caps limit the bill to 1% of gross assessed value for a homestead, 2% for other residential and farmland, and 3% for nonresidential property. Without the homestead deduction you do not get the 1% cap.

faqs.q: Does a flood or storm repair affect the sale of a house in Elkhart County?
faqs.a: It can. Buyers and inspectors look at past water damage, so keep receipts and permits. The Elkhart River reached a record 13.2 feet in February 2018, and drainage and basement history comes up in most inspections.
